x-meta.usage:
Set this when the account is created through a hosted authentication form and you already know which mailbox the user is supposed to connect, so a user cannot finish the form against a different account than the one you provisioned.

For OAuth2 the address is compared against what the provider reports, never against anything the caller supplied, so for a shared or delegated mailbox this has to be the authenticating principal rather than the mailbox address. For IMAP it is compared against the address typed into the form, which the credentials do not prove ownership of.

The constraint stays on the account and is enforced again on every later reauthentication.

path.description: Mailbox folders to monitor for changes (IMAP only). Use "*" to monitor all folders (default)

x-meta.usage:
Leave this at `"*"` unless the account is large and you only care about a few folders. Narrowing it reduces the number of folders EmailEngine keeps open and indexes, which is the main cost of syncing a big mailbox.

Unmonitored folders stay fully reachable through the API. What you give up is webhooks: nothing is emitted for changes in a folder that is not on this list.

disableIMAP4rev2.description: Do not use IMAP4rev2 even if the server supports it

x-meta.usage:
Set this only after a server has actually misbehaved. A handful of IMAP servers advertise IMAP4rev2 support and then answer incorrectly, and this forces EmailEngine back to IMAP4rev1 for that account.

It has no effect on accounts that authenticate with OAuth2.

resyncDelay.description: Delay in seconds between full mailbox resynchronizations

maxIdleTime.description: Restart IDLE after this many milliseconds. Also caps the polling interval for servers without IDLE support.

x-meta.usage:
Leave this unset unless the server, or something between it and EmailEngine, drops idle connections. Some providers close an IDLE session after a few minutes without saying BYE, which shows up as a reconnect every few minutes. Set a value below that limit, for instance 120000 for a connection that drops after about four and a half minutes, and EmailEngine ends and restarts IDLE that often, so the connection never looks idle.

A handful of providers (Yahoo, Rambler, 163.com) already get a built-in value; one set here takes precedence over it. Unlike `disableIMAP4rev2` it also applies to accounts that authenticate with OAuth2. Changing it reconnects the account.
